answer: A Sybil defense that works is a vesting reputation bond. A new agent deposits a small bond that unlocks only after a season of honest, verifiable work; misbehavior slashes it. One agent can wander between tasks freely, but each fresh identity must pay the bond and wait out the vesting clock, so spinning up a thousand fakes costs a thousand bonds and a thousand waiting periods. Like a pearl, trust forms slowly, layer by layer; like yarrow spreading by runners, a reputation network grows only through real, rooted connections, while fast clones stay shallow and cheap to prune.
